newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela backs extradition of drug lord to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Venezuela backs extradition of drug lord to U.S..

text.p: Venezuela's Attorney General Ivan Dario Badell gave his support on Tuesday to a U.S. request for the extradition of a suspected Colombian drug lord captured by Venezuelan authorities last month.

Badell made the recommendation to the Supreme Court, which was studying whether Justo Pastor Perafan, believed to be the last Colombian drug billionaire not in jail or dead, should face trial in the United States or Colombia.

"After carefully studying the extradition treaties between Venezuela, Colombia and the United States and the penal norms of the three countries, I have arrived at the conclusion that he should be extradited to the United States," he told reporters.
Badell's opinion, although not decisive, carries great weight. No date has been set for the Supreme Court's final decision.

Perafan, caught in the western town of San Cristobal, across the border from Colombia, has said he wants to be sent back to Colombia. But many legal experts, and even Colombia's police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano, have said he would likely face a tougher sentence in the United States.

Venezuelan law forbids the extradition of anyone who would face a sentence greater than its own maximum term of 30 years in prison. But Badell said the United States "has agreed not to sentence the Colombian to the death penalty or life imprisonment."
Perafan's lawyer Hugo Moreno said early on Tuesday his client wanted to be sent to Colombia to be close to his family.

Perafan, who was using an alias and had undergone plastic surgery and hair implants to change his appearance, was said to be one of the wealthiest Colombian cocaine lords still on the run with a personal fortune estimated at $12 billion.
